sources.title: NJ utilities board votes to keep electricity rates level
sources.text: NJ utilities board votes to keep electricity rates level
sources.highlight: NJ utilities board votes to keep electricity rates level
sources.after: The Board of Public Utilities approved a series of rate changes Thursday that will keep rates roughly level for residential electric ratepayers while shaving dollars off most residential gas customers’ monthly bills.

sources.title: New Jersey Releases New Report Outlining Strategic PJM Market Reforms
sources.text: New Jersey ratepayers deserve a clear explanation of why their bills are rising and what can be done about it
sources.speaker: Ben Hertz-Shargel, NJBPU President
sources.before: TRENTON, N.J. – August 13, 2026 – The New Jersey Board of Public Utilities (NJBPU) has released an in-depth study finding that the capacity market run by PJM Interconnection (PJM), the regional grid operator, can no longer deliver reliable power at the lowest possible cost, and NJBPU is calling for reforms to improve it.
sources.highlight: “New Jersey ratepayers deserve a clear explanation of why their bills are rising and what can be done about it,” said NJBPU President Ben Hertz-Shargel.
sources.after: “The fastest way to lower bills is getting new power generation built. That requires replacing PJM's unpredictable price spikes with modern rules that attract long-term investment while protecting customers. States must be allowed an active role in PJM governance to ensure wholesale market structures serve the public interest.”

sources.title: NJ utilities board votes to keep electricity rates level
sources.text: Taken together with the items on the agenda earlier this month, these actions will result in no net increase in electricity rates and a slight decrease in gas rates
sources.speaker: Ben Hertz-Shargel, the board's president
sources.before: Thursday’s votes come months after Gov. Mikie Sherrill signed an executive order that directed New Jersey’s energy regulator to modify components of ratepayers’ monthly bills in an effort to keep costs from soaring amid steep increases in electricity demand. Sherrill signed the order during her inauguration as governor in January.
sources.highlight: “Taken together with the items on the agenda earlier this month, these actions will result in no net increase in electricity rates and a slight decrease in gas rates,” said Ben Hertz-Shargel, the board’s president.
sources.after: Among the state’s four electric distribution companies, Rockland Electric Company will see the largest monthly decrease, though overall bills will remain roughly unchanged at each of the utilities. The average Rockland customer using about 650 kilowatt-hours within a billing cycle can expect their bill to decrease by 67 cents, board staff said, and ratepayers with Atlantic City Electric will pay 5 cents less each month. The average Jersey Central Power and Light customer will see their bill drop by 8 cents.

sources.after: On August 25, 2025, the Legislature passed legislation directing NJBPU staff to investigate whether PJM's capacity market – known as the Reliability Pricing Model – is still doing its job, and to report back within a year. Board Staff examined how the market is structured, how it's performed historically, and why it's suddenly producing extreme price swings. They reviewed PJM's own auction data, tracked the region's ballooning demand forecasts, and weighed in on reform proposals already being debated by PJM, other states, and federal regulators.

sources.title: NJ regulators approve virtual power plant, battery storage programs
sources.text: NJ regulators approve virtual power plant, battery storage programs
sources.highlight: NJ regulators approve virtual power plant, battery storage programs
sources.after: The Board of Public Utilities on Thursday unanimously approved the launch of an interim virtual power plant program and the next phase of the state’s energy storage program. The approved programs make up PowerUp New Jersey, the state’s bid to tap into smart devices and smaller-scale battery projects to soften the impact peak demand has on power prices by paying for reductions in power use or stored energy transmitted to the grid.
